source_review.notes: Checked all twelve structured primary references. Current Kubernetes documentation supports ConfigMap data/immutability, environment-variable snapshots, mounted-volume projection, subPath update limits, and API/watch consumption. JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 supports typed structural validation and explicit vocabulary behavior; RFC 6902 supports ordered patch operations and failure semantics. Current CUE documentation supports constraints, unification, validation, deterministic combination, and the distinction from ordinary overriding. Current OpenFeature specification supports typed defaults, provider resolution, evaluation details, context merging/targeting keys, hooks, errors, and observability. Twelve-Factor guidance supports separating deploy-varying configuration from code while the chapter deliberately adds modern type, secret, reload, provenance, and lifecycle safeguards.

Checked tuple, ellipsis, subscript, function, time/instance/request parameters, equality, and predicate notation with balanced repository-compatible GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation separates configuration construction and identity from application compatibility and runtime consumption.

invariant_checking.notes: All declared ownership, secret, composition, validation, identity, binding, delivery, activation, failure, observation, and retirement invariants remain consistent.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no theorem and contains no deductive proof; its model is an assurance structure under schema, renderer, delivery, process, and provider assumptions.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed; semantic-schema completeness, composition, parser, delivery, reload, targeting, telemetry, and human limitations are explicit.

evidence: The executable configuration inventory is labeled synthetic and explicitly disclaims control effectiveness.
Worked ConfigMap, file-watch, dynamic change, feature-provider, compatibility, and retirement cases are framed as scenarios rather than observed production results.
Standards/tool semantics, platform recommendations, formal models, and operational measurements remain distinguishable.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external configuration deployment, reload test, flag experiment, privacy review, incident, compatibility migration, or production telemetry is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently treats configuration as typed executable influence and separates it from code, secrets, and domain data while distinguishing source/effective, publication/delivery/activation, desired/loaded/evaluated, and structural/operational validity.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can classify and contract settings, design schemas, compose deterministically, canonicalize/version, bind deployments, select delivery, implement reload/cache/fallback, govern flags, activate progressively, observe effective state, audit access, migrate schemas, and retire debt.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from classification/contracts through schema, composition, canonical identity, deployment binding, environment/file/API/flag delivery, reload, activation, state observation, governance, migration, and operations. Ten examples cover units, policy constraints, environment snapshots, file reload, cross-fields, progressive dynamic control, stable targeting, provider outage, rollback compatibility, and flag retirement. Five exercises progress from definitions through lifecycle tracing, diagnosis, architecture design, and semantic schema migration, with complete model answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
